messages:
elaine: Quick heads-up — planned soft-swap for router pool A->B tonight during 02:00-03:00 UTC change window. Release notes: https://releases.redwood.ai/rel-2026-03-soft-swap (short notes in thread).

elaine: Why soft-swap: we want a slow 0->20->50->100 ramp with 5m probes between steps, avoid sudden session churn.

maya: noted. pinning old session cookie TTL + sticky fallback on pool A for 30m after final cutover. command I used: `routerctl set-affinity --pool=a --ttl=1800`

chris: Deploy checklist: 1) warm pool B nodes, 2) sync KV caches, 3) start shadow traffic for 10m, 4) ramp. I'm ready to run the warm step at +10m.

tariq: I pushed a tiny config tweak to LB health check timeout (from 2s -> 3s) to avoid flapping on long tails. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/lb-health/234

deploy-bot: scheduled traffic-shift job created by chris. job id `shift-4680123456`. plan: 0% -> 20% (5m) -> 50% (10m) -> 100% (15m). probes: p95 latency, error-rate, tail-queue.

sre-oncall: I'll watch p95 and 5xx rate. Pager threshold: p95 > 300ms sustained 3m OR 5xx > 0.6% rolling 5m -> pager.

chris: Canary decision rules (brief):
```
if p95_increase > +25% over baseline for 2 consecutive mins -> pause and rollback
if error_rate > 0.5% for 3min -> pause
if queue_depth > 3x baseline -> pause
else continue
```

elaine: also note: if session-affinity loss > 1% after the 50% step, we fallback to pool A via `routerctl traffic set 100% --pool=a` immediately.

maya: I'll tail logs for sticky cookie mismatches and emit an alert if > 0.2% mismatches.

deploy-bot: starting warm on pool B now (warm id `warm-4680123456`).

chris: warm healthy, 12/12 instances passed envoy health, caches synced. starting shadow traffic (10m).

deploy-bot: shadow traffic running (10% of requests, not counted for billing). collecting compare metrics.

tariq: seeing small uptick in redis replica lag during shadow (~50ms) — fine but noting.

chris: ramping to 20% in 2m. will post when started.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift step -> 20% started. step id `s1-4680123456`. expected duration 5m.

elaine: monitoring dashboards: p50 stable, p95 +12% but still under pager. error-rate flat.

sre-oncall: no pager for now. keeping eyes on tails.

chris: starting 50% ramp now (10m window).

deploy-bot: traffic-shift step -> 50% started. step id `s2-4680123456`.

maya: observed session cookie mismatch spike to 0.8% at +3m into 50% step. investigating sticky headers.

elaine: decision time — if mismatch >1% for 2 consecutive mins we rollback. maya, what's direction?

maya: mismatch trending down to 0.5% after quick sticky header revert i pushed. looks like transient.

chris: holding at 50% for full 10m window to verify.

sre-oncall: p95 trending up but still within +20%. no automatic rollback.

deploy-bot: step s2 complete. metrics summary: p95 +18% vs baseline, error-rate +0.12%, session_mismatch peak 0.8%.

elaine: green to proceed to 100% ramp. will run a short final probe at 75% for 3m, then 100%.

chris: starting 75% probe.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift step -> 75% started. step id `s3-4680123456`. duration 3m.

maya: mismatch steady <0.3% at 75%. caches warming.

sre-oncall: p95 holding, 5xx low. thumbs up.

deploy-bot: final ramp to 100% initiated. step id `s4-4680123456`.

tariq: executing affinity TTL gown-down: `routerctl set-affinity --pool=b --ttl=3600` so new sessions stick to pool B.

chris: full traffic on pool B. monitoring for 10m quiet window.

sre-oncall: watching. set synthetic probes across eu/us/apac to ensure region parity.

elaine: documenting rollback criteria in runbook snippet inserted into release notes. link above.

deploy-bot: traffic-shift job `shift-4680123456` finished SUCCESS. final metrics: p95 +10% vs baseline, error-rate +0.09%, session_mismatch 0.15%.

chris: thanks all — post-mortem: none. leaving sticky fallback TTL at 1h. will follow up with a short note in release channel. :tada:

maya: I'll remove the temporary lb timeout tweak after tomorrow's low-traffic window.

elaine: excellent job. no rollbacks required. closing change window early at 02:45 UTC.

sre-oncall: marking this event in incident log as SEV0-none-needed, watch closed.
